title: Hub GCSE History Topic Checklist (Aligned to Edexcel 1HI0)
subtitle: Option P1: Spain and the ‘New World’, c1490–c1555

exam_structure.overview: Tests unfolding period narrative across 3 Key Topics. Q1 Explain two consequences (8m), Q2 Write an analytical narrative (8m), Q3 Explain the importance of two events (16m).

sections.title: Key topic 1: Spain reaches the Americas, c1490–1512

topics.title: 1. Spanish exploration
points: Spain c1490: the crusading spirit & foreign ambitions
Columbus’s attempts to gain sponsorship; Queen Isabella: her desire to spread Christianity & sponsorship of Columbus
Columbus’s first voyage of 1492 & the problems encountered

topics.title: 2. Columbus reaches the Americas
points: Columbus’s actions: exploration of the Bahamas & the Caribbean; foundation of La Navidad
Impact of contact with Indigenous peoples: the discovery of gold, relations with the Tainos & Caribs
Impact of rivalry with Portugal & the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494)

topics.title: 3. Spanish claims in the Caribbean
points: Columbus’s later voyages & his role as governor in the Spanish settlement; establishment of the Spanish colony at Santo Domingo (1496)
Effects of Spanish settlement: treatment of Indigenous peoples, effects of smallpox

Development of an imperial policy in relation to the Caribbean: the regulation of further exploration, the establishment of a monopoly on trade, the extension of Spanish authority & the use of slavery; Catholic missionaries

topics.title: 1. The start of an empire
points: Balboa’s claim of Spanish authority over the Pacific (1513)
Conquest of Cuba
Voyage of Magellan & Spanish claim to the Philippines

topics.title: 2. The conquest of Mexico
points: Cortes’s expedition to Mexico in 1519
Key events of the Spanish conquest of Mexico; Montezuma, the war between Aztecs & Tlaxcalans
Capture of Tenochtitlan & the Aztec surrender

topics.title: 3. Impact of Spain in the Americas
points: Cortes’s actions as Governor & Captain-General of New Spain (1523–28)
Consequences of the Spanish invasion for the Aztecs
Founding & significance of a Spanish base at Panama

sections.title: Key topic 3: The Spanish Empire c1528–c1555

topics.title: 1. Pizarro and the conquest of the Incas
points: Contact with the Incas (1528); death of Huayna Capac
Voyage of Pizarro (1530) & war between Atahuallpa & Huascar
Key events of the Spanish conquest of Peru: the Battle of Cajamarca & the capture of Atahuallpa, the revolt of the Incas, the siege of Cuzco (1536–37); impact of the conquest

topics.title: 2. Expansion of empire
points: Viceroys & encomiendas in the Spanish Empire; Las Casas & New Laws (1542)
Significance: discovery of silver in Bolivia & in Mexico; foundation of La Paz (1548)

topics.title: 3. Impact of the 'New World' on Spain
points: Significance: gold & silver for the Spanish economy & to support Spain’s European empire
Impact on Spain of the slave trade & goods from the Americas
Government of the Spanish Empire: House of Trade & Council of the Indies
